definitions.explanation: A real number that cannot be expressed as a ratio of two integers — examples include π (pi), √2, and e. Contrasted with rational numbers ({有理数|ゆうりすう}).

examples.japanese: ⟦{円周率|えんしゅうりつ}→円周率：28786_enshuuritsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{無理数|むりすう}だ。
{無理数|むりすう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{小数|しょうすう}→小数：27356_shousuu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{表|あらわ}す→表す：01868_arawasu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{無限|むげん}→無限：00296_mugen⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{続|つづ}く→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧。
examples.english: When written in decimal form, an irrational number continues infinitely.

examples.japanese: √2⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{無理数|むりすう}⟦である→である：09855_dearu⟧こと⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{古代|こだい}→古代：05324_kodai⟧⟦ギリシャ→ギリシャ：28897_girisha⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{時代|じだい}→時代：01424_jidai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧すでに⟦{証明|しょうめい}→証明：03242_shoumei⟧⟦されていた→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: That √2 is irrational was already proven back in ancient Greek times.

notes:
Compound of ⟦{無理|むり}→無理：01558_muri⟧ (impossible, unreasonable) + ⟦{数|すう}→数：03360_suu⟧ (number) — literally "unreasonable number," a calque of the European term. Used in mathematics from middle school onward.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {無理数|むりすう}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{有理数|ゆうりすう}→有理数：23552_yuurisuu⟧: irrational and rational numbers
- {無理数|むりすう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{含|ふく}む→含む：01982_fukumu⟧: to include irrational numbers
- ⟦{無限|むげん}→無限：00296_mugen⟧⟦{小数|しょうすう}→小数：27356_shousuu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{無理数|むりすう}: irrational number as an infinite decimal

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{有理数|ゆうりすう}→有理数：23552_yuurisuu⟧: rational number — direct antonym; expressible as a fraction
- ⟦{実数|じっすう}→実数：23404_jissuu⟧: real number — the broader category containing both rational and irrational numbers
- {虚数|きょすう}: imaginary number — numbers involving √-1, outside the real-number line
